[RDSC.11.3] **An expression the artefact does not state is refused, and so
is one nested past the format's limit.** A runtime must refuse at load, with
`DS_ERR_DSC_SEMANTIC`, an artefact carrying:

- an `Expr` (`proto/rete_expr.proto#Expr`) with no member of its `kind` oneof
  set;
- a `SlotAssign` (`proto/term.proto#SlotAssign`) with no `expr`;
- an `Action` (`proto/term.proto#Action`) of kind `ACTION_CALL` with no
  `expr`. `ACTION_CALL` is the one kind that reads `expr` ([RDSC.4a.8]), and it
  is the kind's zero, so an `Action` with nothing set is one;
- an `Action` of kind `ACTION_WITHDRAW_BY_ID` with no `withdraw_fact_id`,
  which aims the withdraw at nothing;
- an `Expr` nested deeper than 48. The outermost `Expr` of a test, an action, an
  assignment or a slot's conversion ([RDSC.5.5.9]) is at depth 0, and an `Expr` inside another is one deeper.

None of these has a meaning: an absent expression is not a literal `0`, not
`null`, and not an unassigned slot. The compiler must not emit any of them. It
must refuse, with `DS_VALIDATE_EXPRESSION_TOO_DEEP`, a program any of whose
expressions would lower to an `Expr` nested deeper than 48, so that no program
it accepts becomes an artefact a runtime refuses. Each is a cheap structural need of the loader under [RDSC.9.9], not a defence
against a hostile artefact.
